question.text: Subordinated debt ranks where in the capital structure?

answer.text: Below senior debt but above preference and equity capital, with all debt claims ranking ahead of preference and equity
At the same level as equity
Above all other claims including government taxes

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states subordinated/junior debt ranks after senior debt, secured subordinated debt ranks after secured senior debt, unsecured debt ranks lowest among debt, and all debt claims rank ahead of preference and equity capital. Option B captures that source-listed ranking. The Trap: "Subordinated" places the debt below senior debt, not below equity. It still sits above preference and equity in the payment waterfall, and it does not outrank government tax claims. Note: Earlier wording added a 3-5% yield premium, yield-seeking investor suitability language, and an attractive risk-return marketing line. Those numeric and suitability claims are not directly supported by the checked workbook and have been removed.
